# Chapter Twelve: Silva Qeae Sedes

> *"I will send forth my hunters, any beast or fowl shall be free to fill the bellies of those who are hungry, my hunters shall be a noble breed, sent to honor me in their work of caring for my people."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

The old Tavern smelled of stale hops and tobacco, the acrid scent of the blue hued smoke stung her eyes, Corliss sat in the corner regarding the myriad of old farmers and traders immersed in conversation or avoiding their lives by drowning themselves in draft.

For the last week she had sat upon this same chair trying to understand how she had failed so completely, for the first time since she could remember she had lost her quarry.

The fugitive, aided by another had eluded her, Corliss following every step, tracking there every move. She had found camp sites and signs of their movement.

The Warden had come across some disturbing signs, soldiers and tales of missing children, but once her quarry had descended into the woods, they seemed to disappear,

Her fugitive and his partner were most definitely mages, she had found signs of power, broken trees and smashed branches she had found there initial trail as clear as day, as if they were not hiding themselves at all, but then over the next few days, that trail had disappeared, the tracks becoming lighter until they simply vanished.

Corliss had tried following the trail for two more miles with no tracks she was relegated to broken twigs and branches, then that had dried up, the two simply vanishing as if they had simply flown off into the sky.

Slamming her fist down on the table in frustration the cup of untouched ale jumped, and a few customers glanced at her.

She met their eyes, and they quickly went back to what they were doing. She had been here too long, and she knew it, damn near a month she thought counting the days and wincing, Corliss had sent word to the wardens a week ago and now she simply waited to find out if they would recall her or not, she had, for the first time failed in her duty.

She had no trail; had no leads she was simply done she thought hanging her head in shame. She heard a rustling and an audible grunt as someone sat down across from the Warden.

Looking up she saw the grizzled face of the barkeep his massive frame causing the chair to groan in protest as he settled in, he peered at her over the large grey unkempt beard, studying her silently with the cold blue steel eyes of someone with years of experience sizing people up.

“Warden, I take it you’re still whining about losing your prey?” the man asked but Corliss could see the slight grin underneath the mass of the grey fur beard.

“It’s still busy in here Grim, shouldn’t you be working the bar?” the Warden asked returning the slight smile. Grim chuckled reaching over and taking the ale off the table, tilting the glass back he emptied it in only a few pulls before putting the glass back in front of Corliss and shrugged.

“emperor is dead, they are all drowning there sorrows, as am I, but not for that codger’s death, instead they are afraid of what his wife is going to do with the kingdom, now that she is unchecked” he finished though he showed a small smile, she could make out the worry in his eyes, he too had heard the rumors and the stories, in fact they had discussed them on more than one night while sitting here waiting.

The Warden looked between the glass and Grim “I hope you’re not charging me for that Barkeep, I can tell your all broken up about the death of our glorious emperor” she said and then the slight smile fell off her own face, as she stared out towards the window “my kind has our own reasons for fearing the change,this does not bode well for the Wardens, the Empress has never been a fan” she finished turning to eye him again.

Grim smiled weakly and made a motion with his hand, a few minutes later a plump barmaid came over with two refills and expertly laid them down without spilling a drop, eyeing the old bartender with an annoyed look, she then shot off into the room to serve others.

“Your wife isn’t happy about your break time Grim” Corliss observed and the other man chuckled “She will be okay, besides it won’t get really busy for another two hours, I was tired of looking at you drowning your sorrow in my good ale, as for the Wardens, they will land on their feet, they always do.

I hear troops have been slowly moving north, taking up positions in towns and cities, getting closer towards the Barrens and towards the Northern Dominance, they are securing the population Corliss, but it also looks like they are marching for war” he said, Corliss could see the sorrow and worry in his eyes, most people despised or feared the Silvan’s who lived within the Northern Dominance, there were a lot of stories but few had seen them, Prior to settling down with his lovely wife, Grim had been a trader and had spent more time in the Northern Territories then anyone she had known.

“I wouldn’t worry Grim” Corliss began shifting in her seat to eye a few patrons who had taken an interest in their conversation. As soon as she locked her cold blue eyes on them, they suddenly found something interesting in their Ale to look at. She went back to studying the old Bar Keep.

“The Silvans were more than capable of taking care of themselves” Corliss stated but she felt a small shred of doubt, everyone knew that within the Northern Dominance was the jewel of trade, the City in the Trees, whoever owned that port, owned all trade from the North and it was possible the Empress had her eye on it.

Grim shook his head, changing the subject away from politics. “You have been sitting around here moping for a month, I mean when you first walked in I had no idea what to make of you, but you were quiet and paid your bill, but I have to say now that I have spent enough nights listening to you whine about your first failure, maybe it’s time you put it behind you” Grim said his eyes coming back to focus on the younger woman.

Corliss looked around the bar, it was your typical smoke-filled room mostly dark with small lanterns on each table to illuminate the patron’s food.

She liked it, it was an easy place to get lost in, a place where people keep to themselves mostly coming in to drowned away their daily stress. With a sigh she nodded towards Grim turning back to face him, she had been rattled by her failure, but the old Barkeep was right, she needed to get over it. The Warden had spent a lot of time alone, tracking or surviving in the woods. She didn’t need people, but she liked the atmosphere and the noise, it felt alive she thought enjoying the rooms ambiance as she regarded the barkeep across the table.

“I’ve never failed Grim, we have talked about this before, it’s not something I do and what this guy did was impossible I mean it’s like he sprouted wings” Corliss stated.

She and Grim had hashed this out night after night for the last two weeks, ever since the older man had decided to start sitting with the Warden.

“Everyone fails Corliss, everyone, it’s not the failure that gets you, it’s how you deal with it after” Grim stated leaning forward and eyeing the Warden.

“Why is it you can’t get past it?” he asked, Corliss thought about it, why couldn’t she get by it, it wasn’t like she made a mistake, she had been over that area at least a hundred times if there had been a trail, she would have found it.

Somehow this mage had made their trail disappear, had simply washed away all trace of them, Corliss had never seen anything like it, and then anger set in on her face, her father had never told her she was tracking mages, there was an inherent danger in it, Wardens did not track mages, that was the purview of the Order.

She kept her fear to herself, it could have been he didn’t know the man had been a mage, so it was simply an oversight, otherwise this was just another thing added to the long list of rumors that further showed the disintegration of the territories into war. To Grim she simply shook her head, keeping her thoughts to herself and leaning back in the old wooden chair “Ill get by it Grim, don’t worry about me too much” she said offering a reassuring smile to her new friend.

The old Barkeep just shook his head, he was well practiced in the self-delusion of people and knew nothing he could say would help the woman. The door slammed open and everyone’s eyes except Corliss’s went to it. The Warden watched as the old man’s eyes narrowed his body getting a little tense.

It’s a stranger and one who is armed thought Corliss, extending her hand and gently placing it on the other man’s forearm as he began to rise.

“That would be for me” she said turning to regard the young man in buckskins, his weapons displayed across the large leather belt canted on his hips, as he moved the patrons eyed the small curved blades and pistols he wore.

With a smile Corliss nodded at her fellow warden and motioned for him to join.

Grim got up, sensing this was a conversation best had in private and returned to the bar. The young man nodded at Corliss smiling and then the smile fell as he surveyed the room seeing the hostile and suspicious eyes now locked on him.

The young man ignored the patron’s looks and pushed a string of dark hair out of his face as he made his way over to the table.

Settling in across from Corliss he extended his arm; she grasped his wrist warmly. “Turin, why did they send you out here, Aurtus’s ass man, don’t you have better things to do?” The older warden asked smiling at her friend and one-time apprentice.

Corliss noticed the badge above his left breast as well as the gold ring that now stood out on his finger, the ruby eyes of the raven glinting against the lantern light of the table matching her own ring and nodded approvingly.

“Warden now I see, congratulations my friend” she said warmly. The young man beamed proudly for a moment and then Corliss watched his face fall.

“The Lord Adjudicator asked me to retrieve you, it’s bad Corliss. I don’t know what’s happening, but the entire senior leadership of the Wardens are being called back to the keep, a royal messenger arrived a week ago and since then it’s been like a dark cloud has arrived over the castle” The young man stated still looking nervously around the small inn, the patron’s continuing to regard him with suspicion.

Corliss followed his gaze and then smiled. “Pay no attention to them Turin, they will always be suspicious of new people, it’s a small town, they are not used to strangers and are forever worried about danger, especially when you walk in with your weapons in full view, where is your cloak, didn’t I teach you better than that” Corliss teased eliciting a sheepish grin from his old apprentice.

Corliss’s face went serious “As for the keep, whatever it is, we will get through it, we always do, come let us head out, it sounds as if I am needed” The Older Warden finished. With that she got up and walked over to the bar saying her goodbyes to Grim and dropping a small pile of silverlings on the bar.

Grim nodded at his friend, no words were needed, they both had said everything there was to say. The two Wardens left the inn, walking out into the warm spring air, as night settled over the small village. “We have two days hard ride ahead of us Turin, you need any supplies before we go?” Corliss asked heading for the stables.

The young man shook his head “No I ensured the stable hands loaded me up before I came into the inn” he stated and with an approving nod from Corliss they retrieved the horses and rode out of the village and into the night.

The full moon lit the way as they expertly navigated the young horses over the old trails and pastures that led north through the territory. They rode through the night taking small cat naps on their horses as they pushed further towards the castle.

As the sun crested the horizon bathing the valley in a pink hue, the wardens continued to make good time, riding past small farms and villages, the inhabitants coming out to regard the unusual sight, they kept moving north towards the Wardens Keep.

As the Wardens came to the township of Baumholder, a small village where Wardens often stopped to resupply when out on missions, however something was amiss, Corliss slowed her horse as the two approached the small town, Turin coming to ride next to her, leaning in he whispered, “What’s wrong”.

Corliss held up a hand and pointed at her ear, the young man quieted cocking his head as the sound of a commotion carried to the two Wardens, cautiously they crested a hill bringing the villages outer wall into view.

Stopping the two Wardens spied troops garrisoned outside the small town, the unusual sight of such a large number of soldiers near an insignificant population gave Corliss pause as a small spark of fear rippled through her body.

“Should we go down?” Turin asked and Corliss held up her hand something isn’t right she thought watching the troops closely as smaller groups of soldiers marched off, returning a short time later herding groups young man.

As the small groups of soldiers made it back to the camp a few of them would usher the group of young men into the center of the camp where a corral had been setup. Corliss spotted a tunic and could see the gold lioness of the Empress on them. “Empress guard but what on earth are they doing” She breathed, and Turin just sat shocked on his horse.

After an hour of watching she motioned to Turin and then took off down the hill in a full gallop.

Coming to the edge of the camp she brought the horse to a full stop almost on top of the two soldiers standing guard at the edge of the makeshift camp. “HALT” one called lowering a spear at Corliss in a threatening manner. “I am Corliss Warden of the Northern Territories, what is going on here?” She demanded mustering as much authority as she could.

Curiously it seemed to illicit a sneer from one of the guards. “Not for much longer eh, hey Warden why don’t you come down here, it gets cold at night, and I could use some warming up” one of the guards said to her with a lascivious grin.

The other shot his friend a disgusted look, turning back to Corliss he bowed his head “Warden, I apologize for my friend, we are on the Empress’s orders, perhaps you should mind your own affairs, I am sure your superiors can explain everything” the second soldier said his tone held authority, something she had never heard from a royal guard when addressing a Warden, what is going on here she wondered.

This was odd thought Corliss, never had anyone spoke to a Warden like that, something was very, very wrong. She considered getting off her horse and making the first guard eat his own lance for the comment, she still spied him looking her up and down with a predatory eye, it was getting on her nerves but looking around and seeing the troops and the young men, she finally understood what was happening, the thoughts of the disgusting guard banished from her mind.

“The Empress is conscripting” she breathed and then motioned to Turin, before the soldiers could say or do anything.

The Wardens took off at a full gallop, she had to reach the castle, something very wrong was going on in the territory and whatever it was, had washed up on the warden’s door.

They rode hard until they finally saw the castle’s profile as it rose above the rocky cliffs of the northern mountains. Riding up the Warden’s road Corliss could see a flurry of activity as people scrambled bringing supplies down the road in loaded wagons, what is going on she thought frowning as she watched the convoy of carts.

The two rode finally reaching the gate of the old Castle.

Corliss stormed inside with Turin on her heels. “Where is the Lord Adjudicator” she called to one of the assistants who was furiously directing people with supplies to load them on the empty carts that stood lined up in the courtyard. He looked up surprised and then pointed up.

Corliss nodded and turned to Turin “Get some food, I will be with you after I talk to Uri” she said and then took off up the stairs. Taking them two at a time she reached the top in moments, quickly making her way past the bustling Wardens and assistants as they carried boxes along the terrace. Standing before the large door she slammed her fist against it three times before she heard the bellowing voice of Uri Ammital Lord Adjudicator of the Wardens call out for her to enter.

Corliss did so, entering the large room she found her mentor slumped in a chair on the far side of the room. “What happened Uri” Corliss said not hiding the concern in her voice. Uri, who usually stood tall and proud looked like he hadn’t slept in days, he sat hunched over the table as if a great weight had settled on him and as Corliss entered the other man’s eyes shifted to greet her. “Hello Corliss, I see Turin found you” he said his voice raspy and low, so unlike the powerful baritone that usually emitted from that large frame.

Uri took a breath, seeming to brace himself against his next statement, looking at his old Apprentice and friend he nodded towards the hall. “You have seen what’s going on out there?” he asked Corliss thinking it more a way to start a conversation then an actual comment on the observation.

“What is going on out there Uri, I mean why are all the supplies being moved out and where the hell are they going anyway?” Corliss asked coming to stand across from the big man.

Uri reached beneath the table and pulled out a document, the parchment had been gently refolded, and Corliss could make out the seal from the half that was visible.

“A Royal mandate?” she asked, and Uri simply nodded though the look on his face told her of the defeat. Corliss had never seen a royal mandate; in fact, she had never even heard of one. “What did it say Uri?” she asked gently but knowing that she really didn’t want to know, whatever was in that parchment had made her once boisterous mentor look broken and beaten.

“We are done Lorin, they have disbanded us” he said using her first name for the first time in decades.

“Done, what do you mean done?” Corliss asked she couldn’t believe it, was it even possible.

It had been the Empresses husband’s great-grandfather who had commissioned the Wardens, the rule of law had been absolute there was no way for even another monarch to disband something that the old man had commissioned, or at least she thought that was the case.

“In truth the Warden’s exist in principal, but we are no longer funded from the royal treasury and she has conscripted every apprentice we have, the Wardens are done, We are being annexed to the Empress’s guard, our keep is now going to be used as the forward command base for a war, Corliss, I fear she is going to declare war on the Silvan Nation, I fear our keep will be the launching point for a genocide” he said looking around the large room he had used for close to two decades as his home, his sanctum and Corliss could hear the disgust in his voice.

Then she remembered the supplies, Uri was up to something she thought through everything she had seen, in fact for the past few months she had seen the Wardens stock up on supplies and weapons, what was Uri up to she wondered studying the old man. “Uri, what are you planning?” she asked in a hushed tone, they were alone, and she doubted anyone could hear but walls tended to have ears when treason was spoken aloud, she thought. The old man locked eyes with the younger warden.

“We are not going to become soldiers Corliss, that is not our purpose, we are the protectors and this upstart Empress will not be the end of us, we will protect as we have been honor bound to do for generations, even if it’s against the Empress’s will” he said and Corliss saw the burning hate for the monarch in his eyes, his anger seeping through his defeated demeanor as he spoke.

“Years ago, we secured a small ancient monastery, it had been taken over by bandits, after clearing it out, I have ensured we have kept an eye on it, no one ever came back to claim it after the original inhabitants were slaughtered, we are going there, its defensible and solid, we can setup there and if need be, ride this out, this will not be the end of the Wardens Corliss, the land is descending into chaos at the Empresses behest. The emperor is dead, soldiers move across the land and the Lord Seer’s have gone missing, new appointees have taken over and there is talk they are mages with incredible power, no one dares stand against them.”

He began and Corliss leaned in shaking her head. Then she stopped and looked at Uri, really hearing what he had said. “Is there any word from my father?” she asked bracing herself as Uri met her eyes “Nothing yet, but as soon as I hear, you will be the first to know” he said but his eyes spoke the news, if they did hear it would mean he was dead. Corliss had mixed feelings, she had spent years despising the man, feeling nothing but absolute contempt.

Now for the first time in her life she felt something other than hate for the man who bore her, the feelings of worry for a man who had. thoroughly kept her out of his life gave her pause, she almost considered going after him, to find him but like all Wardens, she had her duties and Galen had his, if she could she would find out what happened to him she would.

But until then, she had the wardens to take care of. “Uri, to stand against the Empress, its treason, we serve the monarchy of this land, think about what you’re saying” she breathed trying to talk sense into her teacher, this was madness Uri was going to get them all killed.

Uri locked his steel grey eyes to Corliss’s crystal blue ones “There are things you don’t know Corliss, but its time you did” he said and standing, he beckoned her to follow.

She obeyed walking with the big man as he left his office and crossed the spacious terrace, they climbed the two floors to the very top of the old keep, the area where they had the hospital, once used during wartime it had long since been vacant, until now she noticed as Women in white smocks and every Warden medic’s she knew ran around caring for people, pausing to view one patient she watched the competent hands of one of the Warden Medics a rune. Encrusted. Glove hovering over the chest of a child as blue light washed over the patient, she didn’t dare disturb him, his face was thick with perspiration as he concentrated on healing the patient.

The floor was packed she noticed, looking from bed to bed seeing old men, women and children some burnt, and others broken.

Crossing over to one bed she came upon a young girl of six sleeping fitfully, Corliss looked the poor girl over noticing the loss of the right leg and half her body bandaged head to toe.

“By Aurtus Uri, what happened?” she asked her shock and horror mounting as Corliss looked from bed to bed and seeing these people broken and beaten.

Uri stood there next to her for a moment letting her take the scene in. “This is all that’s left of the village of Creekside twenty people out of one hundred and fifty souls, The Empress’s soldiers arrived, bringing with them the new Seer and his … things, they announced conscription of all able-bodied young men and that the village would now work towards the good of the empire, farms and businesses would be removed. They protested the removal of the Seer and the directives of this, thing because he was a thing, covered in black markings with eyes as dark as Mephis’s soul, the newly appointed Seer released his creatures they walked like men but with eyes as black as coal moving more like animals.

They attacked with teeth and claws and magic Corliss, these beasts used Magic, they killed maimed and burned, as the people of the village lay dying, begging for mercy, they killed more. Making an example, the Seer had told them this is what would happen to anyone who defied the Empress” Uri stated, and Corliss could hear the bile in his voice as Anger rose in her.

She felt the small spark of outrage as it began to grow, fed by the sight of these people, these victims and soon her hate burned like a furnace. “Uri, we cannot let this stand” she whispered, realizing her fists were clenched hard enough to draw blood from her palms.

Corliss willed her hands to loosen as she took a breath. Uri just nodded in understanding “We are going to disappear Corliss, we are going to wait, we will bring those like these people to us and protect them, wait out this black queen and her demon knights, people will not take this and when they decide to fight back, to rise up, we will be there, we are the law Corliss and no one is above the law, not even the Empress”

he said. Uri stepped forward to lead her through the mass of refugees but paused “There is one more thing that might interest you, many of the villagers were tortured for information, asked about two strangers, one young and one old, both wielding magic, might speak an ancient tongue, using the old man for interpretation” he finished and looked at her pointedly. “I saw the reports as they came in on your search, read the witness accounts, any chance your father was looking for the same people?” he asked.

She paused and thought about it, could it be and if so, what did it mean, who were these people and why did the Empress fear them, or want them so badly as to torture random villagers she wondered, to Uri she shrugged “it’s possible but if it is, she will have next to an impossible time finding them unless she is very lucky Uri”.

He stared at her for a moment, thinking through her words and then nodded “We might want to find them before she does, but right now we have more important priorities” he finished and motioning to her, he walked through the mass of broken and beaten people.

Corliss knew the Empress was the law and by royal mandate anything she did was legal, but Uri was right there was a moral mandate, a higher law and the Empress had crossed it. Whatever was going on, was going to come to a head and Corliss knew Uri wanted to be on the right side, the moral side.

He had always considered himself a good man and the Wardens honorable, capable of only good. Uri was a religious man and she knew he felt the word of Aurtus outweighed that of even an Empress.

Moving through the cavernous floor she peered around the room seeing the destroyed lives, all to make an example of simple people who lived their lives serving this land, people who had no chance to fight back, who had spent generations in service to the crown, this was there payment.

She felt those who had power over others had an obligation to serve those people for whom they had power over. Not to lord over them as if they themselves were some kind of deity. Following this line of thought, the Warden was quickly becoming a believer in her mentor’s cause.

“What’s the plan Lord Adjudicator” Corliss said using Uri’s formal title, the old man turned to her, hearing the determination in her voice and smiled.

She was with him and he knew it. Once Corliss made up her mind it was hell for anyone to try and change it.

They left the upper floor and walked back down to the main foyer as they tried to steer out of the way of the flurry of activity as apprentices and newly minted wardens rushed about with supplies for the caravans.

“Alright Ghost” he began leveling a smile at her, though everyone else used her moniker he rarely did and she smiled up at him warmly, giving him a mock salute “Forty-five Wardens are with us, all of the apprentices and the staff as well, the other twenty have decided to go their own way, but they won’t be reporting to the capital, none of them wish to serve the Empress, not after that.

The place we are going is further north Corliss, I am going to put us on the border of the Northern Dominance”. She paused giving him. Troubled look “Won’t the Sylvans mind us encroaching on their territory Uri, they are not to be trifled with, they are of nature and from the stories no man can beat them in the forests, they are not like us” she finished. Uri winced at that last statement “they are more like us then you know, and it will be fine, trust me on this” he finished and then paused again, motioning up to the floor they had just come from “Did you hear what the villagers are calling the Empress now?” he asked, Corliss thought back to the small tour, but she had been too distracted by the state of them “No” she simply said.

Uri nodded “The Black Queen and her Demon Knights, apparently its spreading” he said smiling at the name, “This too shall come to pass my dear, but until then we seek the aid of the Sylvan in order to survive” his last more an order then a statement and she nodded, knowing when Uri gave an order he seldom could be steered from it and woe the Warden who disobeyed she thought following the big man.

Uri walked to a table in the corner and unfolded a map he had been carrying, once it was open, he swept a hand over the large document.

“They are the central port and the key to the North, without the ability to resupply the airships coming from the north, all trade will essentially shut down, crippling not only Vicor but Dever and Lusor as well, whoever controls that port, controls trade for all of the southern and western dominances, the Silvans are a private people, but they are not a weak people, she has to know it will be a fight, but with that dock the Empress could control trade for most of the region, squeezing off trade to our neighbors would make them weak, while focusing trade to Vicor, if someone was looking to invade Dever and Lusor, it would be the smart opening move” he began and Corliss nodded, He put a finger on the map, tracing lines south of their fortress “there are troops moving towards the border as we speak and I fear that they will not bypass the towns on this or the other side of the border, instead killing and ransacking it for soldiers and supplies, if a war starts, innocents will be massacred” he stated as Corliss counted the towns and villages between the soldiers and the border and winced.

Uri’s eyes softened as he thought about the wounded, Corliss could see the pain in the man’s eyes. “The Empress has already proven what her own people mean to her” He whispered.

Corliss recalled the stories she had heard about the Silvan nation, they had been altered during the time of magic and had since withdrawn, no one had really seen them aside from the ship captains and the stories they told were almost not to be believed, they lived in the trees, opting to exist above the world instead of on the ground, or at least that is what she had heard, her focus finally returning to Uri as he began to speak again.

“The Silvan’s are a private people, the only contact we have is the stories the ship captains tell when returning from the city in the trees, the Sylvans are not like us, they are not only a different country, but a different race Corliss, if the Empress is moving against them, I fear it will be genocide, she has always seen them as a lesser species, she does not consider them people at all, I aim to put us in between the soldiers and those innocent villages along the border, we will not let the Empress slaughter her own people or innocent Sylvans in pursuit of ambition or territory, we will hold the line.

We will move the people out of harm’s way and then bring them along the western line of the territory to safety, all while trying not to put ourselves in the middle of a territorial war, no small order”.

Putting a finger to the map Uri traced a line along the border, bringing it to rest outside of the red skirmish line “We will setup a camp here, giving people of both sides a safe haven from the battle, it will not be easy and we will defend it to the last man, but we will protect this place, let the Empress have her war, I don’t care, just not at the cost of her people, not on my watch.

Meanwhile we will put out word any that need aid can come, any who can fight are more than welcome, we need to take a stand and we will do so there” he finished looking up as if once again seeing the medical unit through the vaulted ceiling.

Corliss could see the man’s steel resolve, he was a protector and had spent his life ensuring the safety of the people, not for his ego or for the emperor but because he loved this land and now those who rule aimed to destroy that peace, to kill those who could not defend themselves simply because they were in the way.

Uri would not let that stand and Corliss felt proud to stand with him, no matter what, she would stand against those who would do evil, those who would slaughter the innocent simply because they thought them insignificant.

“We are going to move tonight, under darkness to the old monastery and setup there. We will stay low and keep our ear to the ground, we will know when to make a move when the time is right” he finished nodding as if convincing himself of the plan. Corliss studied her teacher; it was a loose plan, but she understood all too well that any plan never survived contact with the enemy. “Sounds like a plan Lord, where do you need me?” she asked, and the big man clapped his hand on her back smiling.

Corliss spent the rest of the day coordinating the packing and moving of boxes and other items into the carts as they lined up along the road.

Scouts had been dispersed using the tools of the Warden, they ensured unwelcome eyes weren’t peering where they shouldn’t.

So far, the coast seemed clear, but it wouldn’t stay that way, how long before the Empress figured out, they weren’t coming and then sent out soldiers to find them she mused, stopping to survey the winter swept peaks of the old mountain.

They would not go quietly and once they engaged the soldiers, they would become enemies of the state, hunted like those they themselves hunted. But Corliss knew there was no going back, she had made her decision and would follow Uri anywhere and through anything, he deserved her loyalty, her respect and he had it.

The small army of leather clad protectors awaited the amber light of the moon before beginning the exodus from the mountain, the convoy moving down the narrow mountain road like a cloth clad wooden snake, moving slowly towards the north, Corliss took rear guard and as the last wagon left the courtyard and began its hazardous trek down the winding mountain road, she stopped and regarded the old keep, the place she had called home since she had been a little girl and said her goodbyes.

She did not think she would ever see the place again and tears welled in her eyes, change was part of life, but not all change was happy, or good she thought as she turned her horse to face the road and turned her back on the only place she had ever called home.

They made slow time with the heavily laden wagons and pulled off the road, covering the wagons as best they could as they made camp, putting out scouts to ensure they were not followed the Wardens were now the ones on the run and the irony did not escape Corliss as she slept lightly against the trunk of a tree.

They were on the road at dusk and everything was uneventful until around midnight when the scouts that had been sent again came tearing back to the convoy.

Corliss heard the commotion as she still rode rear guard “Keep the rear” she ordered Turin who rode alongside her and set her horse at a gallop until she found the gaggle of rangers gathered near the center of the convoy.

Voices were excited and panicked, she couldn’t make until she was almost on top of them.

“The village is aflame my Lord; troops are ransacking everything” came the last snippet of conversation as she sidled up next to Uri.

“What’s going on?” she asked looking at the two scouts. The older one, Kolrim was his name Corliss thought began to speak. “The Empress’s soldiers are burning the village ahead, it’s a massacre Corliss” he said, and She could see his haunted eyes.

“Uri, we can’t let this stand” she said as she looked to the Lord Adjudicator.

He sat there for a moment silent, and Corliss felt for him, knew he had a hard decision to make, until now they had only disobeyed the Empress, but not stood against her, this would be crossing the line, there would be no censure or fine but the penalty for what he was contemplating to standing against the empress’s guard, was considered treason, the penalty was death.

Uri knew if he ordered it the Wardens would defend the village but in doing so, he would be signing their death warrants, all of them so he sat their indecision causing his silence. Corliss had enough, they could not let this stand.

“Mephis’s ass, I am going Uri, you can try and stop me” she said and then standing up on her horse she yelled as loud as she could.

“Villagers are being killed by empress’s guard, who will go with me to defend them?” she asked and out of the convoy came every Warden there and Corliss smiled with pride.

A few moments later an army of forty rode hard towards the light in the distance, the burning of the houses and buildings a beacon to guide their way.

The Wardens came over the hill in a line, one of them was prepared for what they saw.

It was like hell had opened on earth, buildings lit the village as soldiers lined, shadowy figures amongst the burning pyres, lines of villagers the young and old alike stood in lines and were quickly felled by the soldier’s rifles, the bodies falling in a row to be added to those already dead.

Whatever the soldiers were doing they were not taking prisoners Corliss observed as the heat of anger rose in her belly stoked by the vision of horror in front of her.

“Wardens, ride” Corliss yelled as she spurned her horse into a full gallop, the scream breaking her fellow wardens out of there horrific trance, they too rode like the Valkyries of old, they descended upon the battlefield swooping into the midst of the death and devastation.

Corliss let go the reigns pulling the pistols from her belt, she took aim and fell two soldiers who fought over a young girl, her dress half torn to reveal a bruised and bloody naked breast.

She let lose all twelve shots, blue bolts of energy finding their targets as Soldiers dropped before her, stowing the guns, she reached around to the small of her back, pulling the backup pistols, more bolts of energy flew from her barrels as she dropped ten more soldiers who stood at the left end of the firing line, replacing those.

Pulling the Hatchets from the harness on her lower back, she rode down upon the soldiers, anger fueling her determination, springing from the horse, amidst the blue bolts of returning fire, she used the horse’s momentum to launch herself, slamming knees first into the closest soldier, riding him to the ground before rolling and coming up on her feet.

Quickly Corliss was in among them before the soldiers knew what hit them.

Bringing the first hatchet up in an underhanded swing she heard the meaty thud as it connected with the underside of a soldier’s jaw.

Over his shoulder she watched as another soldier began to raise his rifle, his eyes as wide as saucers as he began to shakily take aim.

With a quiet curse she launched the second hatchet at the soldier, taking him in the center of the chest.

He went down quickly and before the soldier had hit the ground the mahogany hilt of the old sword was in her hand and swinging like a farmer expertly sowing wheat.

Corliss moved like a dancer with angelic grace as she dodged and parried blades and daggers, more bolts of blue energy framed the scene adding an otherworldly light to the dance.

A young warden in the thick of battle looked over and stopped, staring in amazement as the woman moved from soldier to soldier slicing and stabbing with the fluid grace of one who had trained all her life, the same grace that had earned her the nickname ghost, she seemed to float ethereally over the field. It was as if she just appeared next to her target, one second there and the next not and they quickly fell to the ancient blade.

She danced with the wood and metal like an expert musician playing at the top of her game. She finished another soldier and looked to her left to see a lone man in the Empress’s tunic carefully aiming the single shot resin rifle, following his target she saw Turin as he parried and lunged with two soldiers, his movements unsure but his form solid as he battled with the guards.

Corliss cursed knowing there was no time to get to the soldier before he fired on her apprentice.

Flipping the blade she held it like a spear and with a grunt threw the blade, holding her breath time seem to slow as the blade arced in the air flying straight and true, the soldier never got the shot off as the sword pierced his neck burying itself halfway in, she watched the man drop.

Corliss almost missed the sound of the blade swinging down upon her as she looked to see how Turin was faring. At the last minute she felt more than heard the soldier as he swung his sword in a downward arc. Jumping back Corliss felt the air as the blade barely missed her.

Quickly bringing her foot down on top of the blade as the soldier overextended his swing, she drove the sword into the ground. Bringing up her elbow she slammed it into the soldier’s face.

Grabbing his arm, she used it as leverage to do a half somersault swinging both her legs around his neck, locking them, she arched her back, flipping him end over end and slamming the man’s head on the ground as she landed on her back with a grunt.

Still holding his arm, she twisted, locking the elbow and then wrenching it until she heard the loud pop of the shoulder.

Corliss jumped to her feet and watched as the Wardens finished off the last of the soldiers and then they were standing there among the dead.

Corliss began walking around checking the bodies of the villages, looking for any who might be alive.

She hooked her fingers in her belt as she did, hiding the shaking in her hands as the adrenaline wore off. Surveying the bodies of men women and children shot dead and left on the ground.

As the wardens scrambled to aid anyone left alive, the convoy came over the hill parking near the village so that the others could aid the victims.

They spent most of the day putting out fires and bandaging the few left alive. When all was tallied, they had killed seventy soldiers and of the nearly one hundred and sixty villagers who lived there, only seven were alive.

Corliss sat near an old man as the medic bandaged his wounds. Tears rolled down his cheeks as he stared at the now covered bodies of his daughter and granddaughter.

“They showed up, telling us that we were to move to the nearest town, we were to be conscripted as labor for the Seer’s new metal plant, when we refused, they tried to force us, but we resisted. The captain said they needed an example so no one else would resist and that’s when they started killing, the Empress guard Warden, they always protected us, but they killed my daughter and my granddaughter, to make an example” he cried, and Corliss shared the man’s pain.

Tears welling in her own eyes as she listened to his story. What had happened to this land, what madness was this she thought trying to understand actions that made no sense to her.

They had always protected the people of Vikor, they were sworn to defend them as were the Empress’s guards.

How was it possible that they now slaughtered the people they were sworn to protect, what had happened to the world she thought trying to wrap her head around this.

Uri walked up motioning her to join him,

She crossed the small area looking over to the small market building that had once been the place all the villagers would get supplies, now nothing more than a smoking pile of charred ash.

“We have to move, we are going to take two of the wagons and hide the supplies, we will use it to move the wounded and take them with us, but we cannot be here when more soldiers arrive” he said looking out over the hill as if any moment soldiers would crest it.

Corliss understood, if they were here when the soldiers came, they would be slaughtered, the Wardens were not setup to fight, there were too many innocents and noncombatants, there number would be set to protect and defend those, thus making them easy targets.

They hurriedly bandaged and stabilized the villagers, hiding supplies in the wooded tree line and covering them so they could come for them later. Once they were loaded up the convoy was moving, Uri doubled the scouts the gravity of what was happening finally hitting all of them.

Corliss looked around and could see it on their faces, the worry and the shock of the last two days slamming home had taken its toll on everyone. It was another four days until the convoy crested a final rise.

An old squat stone complex that had seen better days emerged in front of them, nestled in the tree line and half covered with ivy it looked as if the wilderness had already taken the structure back.

“It’s going to need some work” Uri stated almost apologetically as he rode up behind Corliss. She simply laughed gently, “Home is home Uri; home is home we will get it fixed” he simply nodded as the two slowly rode next to the convoy as they approached the ancient monastery.

Dismounting the horses outside the gate, the big man let his steel eyes rove over the outside of the once proud complex, Corliss could see where a garden had been and from the look of it the soil was still viable, that would allow them to grow food next season to help feed the wardens.

The approaches mostly in the open, so no one was sneaking up on them she thought looking to see the rear was backed up against forest, then reassessed as she spied the old broken and crumbling wall, they would need to fix that first she thought with a nod.

There came a rustling and Corliss caught something large flitting between branches, disturbing a flock of birds and other ariel predators as she watched a small group of snake’s flit from the trees, there membranous wings carrying them over the tree top, whatever it was, it was fast and agile she thought squinting as Corliss lay her hand on the grip of the pistol her thumb releasing the strap.

She felt a hand gently lay on top of it and looked up to see Uri smiling at her. “They have been with us for a while my dear, if they wanted us dead understand we would not be standing here” he finished, Corliss was about to ask what they were when something resembling a man stepped from the shadow of the ancient wall surrounding the complex.

His eyes were bright blue and twice the size of a normal humans, the man stood about five foot nine with a long mane of green tinted white hair, its skin was bronze and it moved with a fluid grace that told Corliss that this creature was light on its feet and fast, its legs arms looked gangly and thin as if they were just a little too long for his frame, she looked over its body, seeing the three fingers that were twice as long as a man’s and terminated in long narrow claws, it wore a leather outfit with fittings of silver but no shoes, instead its bare feet were elongated, with toes that also terminated in claws, the foot was bent oddly like that of a dog she though “Silvan” she whispered putting the stories to the man standing in front of her.

Uri nodded next to her Corliss catching it out of the corner of her eye “they are called the Silv Quea Sedas, or Silva for short”, He whispered as the man, stood there silently regarding the two of them.

Uri stepped forward a smile spreading across his face the Silva mimicking him.

“General Durass, I take it your scouts are above somewhere looking down on us?” he asked, and Corliss could hear the playful tone in his voice. Durass nodded “Since you left that last village my friend, it’s good to see you again” the gentle voice said. Corliss looked up at first seeing nothing, then she caught movement, and again, and again her eyes adjusting to the low light of the shadows within the trees and then with a gasp she saw, close to fifty of the Silva nestled in the tree, some hanging upside down, some squatting on the branches, but all regarding them silently, carefully.

“This is my protégé Lorin Corliss” Uri said calling her over and breaking her from the trance.

She smiled as she moved towards the General, how did Uri know him, as he had said, no one had seen the Silvan’s except for those traders going through the northern port, as she came to stand before him the Silvan smiled, the action genuine as he bowed over her hand “Kiur domotre” he whispered “Good to meet you Warden Lorin Corliss, any friend of Uri, is a friend of ours” he said bowing slightly.

“Well met sir” Corliss stammered out looking between the two men.

“Ah yes, Uri has talked much about you child, it is good to finally meet you, I and my brethren thank you for coming to our aid” he said bowing slightly over her hand once again.

Corliss looked over the Silva’s shoulder as light thumps sounded from around the trees and as she watched, the Silva dropped from distances of twenty feet or more to land on the ground easily and with such grace.

The scouts came to stand loosely and at ease waiting on their General.

Durass turned to address his men and Corliss leaned in “I have heard stories, but I never believed them true, how is this possible, I mean why are they. like that” she asked, and Uri nodded.

“When the second age of man came, some that landed took to the forest, one such man was an expert in the building blocks of man, the small group decided because they wished to start fresh, they would alter themselves, but for a long time without the equipment, they floundered, until they discovered they had the gift, for many decades there leader honed his abilities until he was able to alter those over only a few generations into men who could live as one with nature, men with the strength to master the forest” he said, pausing the discussion as Durass returned.

“My men will setup patrols while your people begin to repair the abbey” Durass said and with a wave of his hand, the Silva dispersed into the trees, leaping gracefully into the trees they went, using the trees almost like squirrels they disbursed into the forest.

Despite the unsteadiness of the last few days and the emotional rollercoaster of being abandoned by the Crown, Corliss looked over the Wardens and then to Durass.

She knew in her heart they were doing right, that they were on the right side of this. They might die for their beliefs, but they would enter the afterlife with their heads held hi she thought.

She came to sit at one of the fires the Wardens had begun to set as the sun retreated for the day and sat there reflecting on the incredible nature of the Silva when General Durass came over, sitting across from her, his large blue eyes seeming to glow in the firelight as he smiled regarding her.

“I can imagine my visage is a bit unsettling, fear not for we mean you no harm Warden” he said gently proffering the warden a warm smile.

Corliss shook her head. “Forgive me, I do not think you mean us harm, any friend of Uri is a friend of mine, I have never seen your like before, I apologize if it’s that obvious, I do not mean to stare” she said trying to convey her embarrassment but Durass leaned his head back and laughed.

“To you we must look odd, it is one of the reasons we keep to the North before the pact was signed, the one that gave us the Northern Dominance and gives you access to the docks, the then Empower would send expeditions into the forest trying to capture us, thinking us some kind of wood nymph, it almost led to war, until a very, very young soldier managed to save a very young and dumb warrior who thought he would gain honor my capturing him”.

Durass said and Corliss squinted. “Do you mean you and Uri?” she began and Durass nodded “We have known each other for a long time my dear, it was because of his arguments to his commander that the first steps towards the pact were made” he finished.

Corliss looked to the trees where the muted glow of simians jumped from tree to tree, it was a common sight in the forests but still gave the dark woods a spectral feel.

“We never see your people in the other dominances, the only thing we have is the stories the sailors come back with, even the Winter War is merely a byline in history” she stated focusing her attention back on the man’s unusually large eyes.

“We keep to ourselves, we are the guardians of the north, it was part of the pact, the soldiers who ventured beyond our territories were never heard from again, there are things beyond even our borders that would be the thing of nightmares, we keep them from humanity” he stated his smile faltering for a moment. “The Empress threatens the peace, threatens breaking the pact and I fear she does not know the ramifications of such a decision, all she sees is the acquisition of the Northern port that will let her control the trade for most of your people between the other dominances” he finished and Corliss nodded.

Durass looked towards the woods. “There are other kinds of men, if you want to call us that, that live within the barrens, but ours is the territory that borders yours so we are your only experience with those who altered themselves to be closer to the land” he finished and Corliss thought about asking more but looking at him, she got the sense it was not a subject that was open for discussion. Instead they both sat in a companionable silence watching the flames.
